final.disposition: widen_existing (check 3), merged with the other check-3 widening. Check 3 today asks one question: does a gated assertion execute on the lane that gates the PR. Wade's record shows the wider theme: before he approves a hardware-path or scheduler-path change, he wants evidence that a run exercised the changed path at the reviewed head, in every build configuration the diff touches. When the PR makes a test statement that does not cover the changed path, he asks the author (2915270383: one runtron command named while the hunks sit under `#ifdef FWD_HW_RESULTS`; 4265644124: a test plan of clang-format and whitespace only; 3156090573: a `--users 1` repro under a bot finding about duplicate shards). Twice he ran tests himself and pasted the result: a full ctest summary of 69 tests (4131374395) and a `Running t_... PASS` list of 13 binaries (4422833076). On all four member heads the gating lane `CMake and CTest` (cmake-single-platform.yml) produced no ctest run (verified with gh api): at 8f22c93862 and 9d0d649274 the workflow did not run at all because its `pull_request: branches:` list omitted the base branch (hwattention_sync at 8f22c93862; wm-bill-hwsync1 at 9d0d649274); at e76638c63e, 1d3ff17c9d and 159e09a940 `lint | failure` skipped the `build` job (`needs: lint`), which held the ctest steps. The row named `test` on those heads is the job `test` of test-release-build.yml, gated by the label `Continuous integration`, which none of the four PRs carries; it says nothing about ctest and is not read by this check. The widening keeps the existing trigger as Trigger A and adds Trigger B (insufficient test statement at HEAD). The heading is shared with the item test-silently-skips-or-cannot-fail, which also widens check 3 under Trigger A; this item owns Trigger B only.

skill_entry.name: 3. A check on the changed path must execute, and a run must be named, at the reviewed head
skill_entry.trigger: Trigger A (unchanged): a runtime assertion on stored bytes or indices sits below a runtime exit on a hardware or environment probe. Trigger B, all three: (1) the diff changes non-comment, non-formatting lines on a hardware-facing path (h/pos/, src/pos/, h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp, h/tron/scheduler/), a production constant (timeout, sentinel), or a region under a defined macro whose `#else` or `#ifndef` twin reads an identifier the hunk assigns; (2) the job that runs ctest has no success row at HEAD; (3) the PR text (body, commits, comments) makes a test statement that does not cover the changed path: static checks only, one named run beside such a gated hunk, or a repro whose flags exclude the runtime scenario a High-severity bot finding names.
skill_entry.procedure: Trigger A: steps 1-8 unchanged. Trigger B: merged PR: BASE from `.base.sha`. Read the check runs at HEAD; find the job whose step runs `ctest` or `bin/slice run`; ignore the row named `test` (test-release-build.yml, label-gated). State the cause: `needs: lint` after a lint failure, or a `pull_request: branches:` filter omitting the base. Map each hunk to its preprocessor region by script; grep the twin for the identifiers the hunk assigns. List tests by link line in t/CMakeLists.txt (`pos` library, `LABELS fpga`, `DISABLED TRUE`). Collect test statements from body, commits and comments; match each to a configuration. Keep bot findings at HEAD that name a runtime scenario. With a labelled host run and paste the summary; otherwise `Insufficient data`.
skill_entry.question: Which run, named by binary or command, by build configuration and by commit, executed the changed path at this head, and where on the PR does it say so? If a changed hunk sits under `#ifdef X` and the twin region reads the state the hunk writes, did a build with X in the opposite state compile and run too?
skill_entry.do_not_fire: A PR with no test statement in body, commits or comments (Wade approved 2135, 2008 and 1827 in silence: same author and base as 2148, lane never ran). Comment-only, test-only, documentation-only and one-line PRs. A ctest job that succeeded at HEAD when no gated twin reads the hunk's state. Formatting-only hunks (`git diff -w` empty). Regions under a commented-out or never-defined macro (`// #define MORE_HWATTN_DEBUG`). Static bot findings (sizeof, bound, duplicate constant): verify-automated-findings owns them. `(Disabled)` rows in a ctest summary. `#if 0` blocks the author still needs. A WIP body on a feature-branch base. A run cited at an older id: check 8 owns it. Never block: the strongest form is a conditional approval or a question.
skill_entry.finding_shape: 'do these changes for <feature> work when `<MACRO>` is UNdefined as well? Did you sanity test that?' or 'Approved, but please run at least a subset of representative UTs (<binaries from the link line>) against these changes before merging.' or, under a bot finding that names a runtime scenario, 'I think this is a legit concern... did you run any <multi-user | repeated-iteration> tests to see if you encounter this issue?' With a labelled host, state the result instead: 'all the UTs pass out of this branch as well:' followed by the pasted summary (`100% tests passed, N tests failed out of M`, the Label Time Summary and the `(Disabled)` rows).
skill_entry.severity_wade_uses: normal, as a question or as a condition on an approval, never a block (0 CHANGES_REQUESTED in 334 reviews): "Approved, but please run ..." (4265644124; review state COMMENTED at 1d3ff17c9d, the prose says Approved; the APPROVED state is 4339065826 at 159e09a940 ten days later with an empty body), "Did you sanity test that?" (2915270383), "I think this is a legit concern" (3156090573). When he has the machine he states the result instead of asking: "all the UTs pass out of this branch as well" (4131374395, a 69-test ctest summary) and "The following set of UTs ran/passed against these changes" (4422833076, 13 binaries).
skill_entry.evidence_scope: hunk (the changed region and its macro), full file (the `#else` or `#ifndef` twin and the identifiers it reads), other files (t/CMakeLists.txt link lines and labels; the other files that test the macro), PR body plus commit messages plus comments (test statements, runtron repro flags), CI (check runs at HEAD; the job whose step runs ctest or bin/slice run; the workflow `on:` block and `needs:` lines), bot findings at HEAD with a runtime scenario, runtime (the run itself; needs a host with the hardware label and a build of HEAD).

Enclosing region of each hunk, by script: hunk starts `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- <f> | grep '^@@' | sed -E 's/^@@ -[0-9,]+ \+([0-9]+).*/\1/'`; for each start L: `git -C WT show HEAD:<f> | awk -v L=$L 'NR>L{exit} /^#(ifdef|ifndef|if)[ \t]/{d++;n[d]=$0;s[d]=NR;next} /^#else/{n[d]=n[d] " [else@" NR "]";next} /^#endif/{d--;next} END{for(i=1;i<=d;i++) printf " > %s@%d", n[i], s[i]; print (d?"":" top level")}'`.
10c. For each macro X that encloses a hunk: the macro counts only when it is defined by an uncommented `#define X` in the file or by a CMake, preset or `-D` line (`git -C WT grep -n -E 'define X|-DX' HEAD -- CMakeLists.txt CMakePresets.json nix h src`); `// #define X` is not a configuration. The region counts only when X has an `#else` or `#ifndef X` twin in the file and the twin reads an identifier the hunk assigns: identifiers `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- <f> | grep '^+' | grep -o -E '[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*(\[[^]]*\])? *(=|\.wait|\.data)' | sort -u`; twin read `git -C WT show HEAD:<f> | sed -n '<else>,<endif>p' | grep -n -E '<ident1>|<ident2>'`. Record how many other files test X (`git -C WT grep -l '<X>' HEAD -- h src`). An in-file `#define` means every run named on the PR used the defined state unless a sentence says otherwise.
11. Tests that can reach the touched code, from the link line: `git -C WT show HEAD:t/CMakeLists.txt | grep add_catch_test | grep -E 'LIBRARIES[^)]*\b(pos|full_scheduler)\b'` (binaries that link the real hardware library; 22 at 8f22c93862); `grep -E 'LABELS fpga'` (need a card; 21); `grep 'DISABLED TRUE'` (never run; 6). 12. Test statements on the PR: body `grep -n -i -E 'tests passed|Running t_|ctest|runtron|make gen/|clang-format|whitespace|\[x\]|\[ \]|validated|tested' body.md`; comments and reviews `gh pr view N --repo positron-ai/tron --json comments,reviews --jq '.comments[].body, .reviews[].body' | grep -n -i -E 'tests passed|Running t_|ctest|runtron'`; commit messages `git -C WT log --format=%B BASE..HEAD | grep -n -i -E 'tests passed|Running t_|ctest|runtron|validated|tested'`. A run counts only when it names a binary or a command and a configuration; "Validated out to 40100 tokens of context" (PR 2148 commit 667a2619e5) is a claim without a command. One runtron command is one configuration and, with `--users 1` or `--iterations 1`, one user or one iteration only. No test statement at all: do not fire.
13. Bot findings at HEAD only: `gh api repos/positron-ai/tron/pulls/N/comments --paginate --jq '.[] | select(.user.login|test("bot")) | select(.body|test("High Severity")) | "\(.id) \(.commit_id[0:10]) line=\(.line) \(.path) | \(.body|split("\n")[0])"'`. Keep only findings that name a runtime scenario (multi-user, repeated iterations, long prompt, concurrent requests) and compare with the repro flags from step 12. A static finding (sizeof, bound, duplicate constant) goes to verify-automated-findings.
14. Report per (configuration, label set): run named at HEAD (cite) or none. A run cited at an older commit id is check 8's finding; name it there, do not repeat it here.
15. With a build of HEAD on a host that has the labels: run `ctest -L fpga` or the step-11 binaries and paste `100% tests passed, N tests failed out of M`, the Label Time Summary and the `did not run (Disabled)` rows verbatim.
